how.title: From pixels to
how.copy: Useful basketball analysis depends on more than detecting a player in one frame. CourtFlux is structured around temporal continuity: what is on screen, where it moves, what persists, and how those observations can later support possessions, events and tactical interpretation.

image.alt: CourtFlux workflow showing basketball video progressing from object tracking toward tactical insight

steps.title: Video becomes tracked objects.
steps.copy: Player detections, team classification and ball candidates create the first structured layer above raw footage.

steps.title: Frames become trajectories.
steps.copy: Tracking across time matters because basketball decisions happen through movement, occlusion, transitions and changes of possession.

steps.title: Trajectories become basketball evidence.
steps.copy: As the product develops, spatial mapping, possessions, events and tactical patterns can build on a stronger tracking foundation.

capabilities.eyebrow: What is available vs what is coming
capabilities.title: A basketball analysis stack built
capabilities.copy: CourtFlux does not present future basketball intelligence as if it were already production-ready. The current beta concentrates on the computer-vision foundation required for later structured analytics.

ball.title: The ball is small on screen but
ball.copy: Possessions, passes, shots, rebounds and turnovers all depend on knowing where the ball is and maintaining continuity when it is briefly hidden. CourtFlux combines direct ball detections with temporal association and conservative short-gap prediction rather than treating every frame independently.
ball.note: Ball quality remains an active benchmark area. CourtFlux does not claim perfect tracking across every camera condition.

faq.question: What is basketball video analysis software?
faq.answer: Basketball video analysis software helps coaches and analysts turn game footage into structured information they can review. CourtFlux is being built to extract player, team, ball and eventually spatial and event context directly from video.

faq.question: Do I need a special camera system?
faq.answer: CourtFlux is designed around normal basketball game film rather than a proprietary capture system. Analysis quality still depends on factors such as camera position, resolution, visibility, occlusion and motion blur.

faq.question: What does CourtFlux analyse today?
faq.answer: The current beta focuses on player detection and tracking, team classification, ball detection and temporal ball tracking. Court mapping, possession segmentation, basketball events, player attribution and tactical intelligence are being developed in stages.

faq.question: Can I analyse a short basketball clip instead of a full game?
faq.answer: Yes. CourtFlux uses analysis minutes based on processed video duration, so a short clip consumes only its own duration rather than being treated as a full game.

faq.question: Is CourtFlux for individual coaches or whole organisations?
faq.answer: CourtFlux currently supports individual and single-team workflows. Broader multi-team academy workflows are part of the product direction and remain in development.
